lesson.text: Remember? Every text has a main idea and details. Today we read two texts on one topic and compare them: what is the same, and what is different?
Text A, a fact page: Emperor penguins are the biggest penguins. They live in Antarctica. The father keeps the egg warm on his feet for about two months, while the mother feeds at sea.
Text B, a scientist's diary: 15 June. It is dark nearly all day here in Antarctica, and −30 °C. I watched hundreds of penguin dads huddle together, each with an egg on his feet.
Compare: both texts say the fathers keep the eggs warm on their feet. Only text A says emperors are the biggest penguins. Only text B tells how cold and dark the winter is.

Stories by the same writer often share characters. Story 1, Pip's Kite: on a windy spring day in the park, Pip's new kite got stuck in a tree. Nell found a long stick, and together they gently shook it free.
Story 2, Nell's Sled: on a snowy hill in winter, Nell's sled cracked. Pip fetched planks and rope, and together they mended it before sunset.
Compare the stories. The settings are different: a windy park, a snowy hill. The plots are alike: a problem, then a friend helps. And the theme is the same: friends help each other.
Try it in the world: read two cards about the same place in the game's Books, like two planets. What is the same, and what is different? Next: prefixes, suffixes and syllables.

exercises.prompt: What do both penguin texts say?
exercises.hint: Find a fact in text A that is also in text B.
choices: The fathers keep the eggs warm
The mothers sit on the eggs
exercises.explain: Both texts say the fathers keep the eggs warm on their feet.

exercises.prompt: Which text is a diary?
exercises.hint: A diary has a date and says I.
exercises.explain: Text B has a date, 15 June, and the writer says "I watched".

exercises.prompt: Both stories have Pip and Nell in them.
exercises.hint: Who is in each story?
exercises.explain: True: the same characters are in both stories.

exercises.prompt: Where does Story 1 happen?
exercises.hint: Look at the setting of Pip's Kite.
exercises.explain: Story 1 happens on a windy spring day in the park.

exercises.prompt: Which fact is ONLY in text A?
exercises.hint: Check each fact against both texts.
exercises.explain: Only text A says emperors are the biggest penguins.

exercises.prompt: Which fact is ONLY in text B?
exercises.hint: Which fact comes from the diary?
exercises.explain: Only the diary tells us the temperature.

exercises.prompt: How are the plots of the two stories alike?
exercises.hint: What happens in each story?
choices: A friend helps solve a problem
exercises.explain: In both, something goes wrong and a friend helps.

exercises.prompt: What is different in the two stories?
exercises.hint: Where and when does each one happen?
exercises.explain: Story 1 is in a windy park in spring; story 2 on a snowy hill in winter.

exercises.prompt: The two stories have the same theme.
exercises.hint: What big idea do both teach?
exercises.explain: True: both teach that friends help each other.

exercises.prompt: What is the theme of both stories?
exercises.hint: The theme is the big idea, not one detail.
exercises.explain: In Story 1 Nell helps Pip free his kite; in Story 2 Pip helps Nell mend her sled. Both show the same big idea: friends help each other.

exercises.prompt: Why might a writer use the same characters in two stories?
exercises.hint: Think of a book series.
choices: so readers can follow them in new adventures
exercises.explain: Readers get to know the characters and enjoy meeting them again.

exercises.prompt: A new text says penguin mothers keep the eggs warm. Which texts disagree with it?
exercises.hint: Who keeps the eggs warm in each text?
choices: both text A and text B
exercises.explain: Text A says the father keeps the egg warm, and text B shows the dads each with an egg on his feet. The new text says the mothers do it, so it disagrees with both.

exercises.prompt: Put the events of Story 2 in order.
exercises.hint: What must happen before the sled can crack?
exercises.explain: Nell sleds, the sled cracks, Pip fetches planks and rope, and they mend it.

exercises.prompt: What is the best way to compare two texts?
exercises.hint: Comparing means looking at both.
choices: Find what is the same and what is different
exercises.explain: List what both texts say and what only one of them says.

exercises.prompt: Two texts on the same topic always give exactly the same facts.
exercises.hint: Did text A tell us the temperature?
exercises.explain: False: each text can give different facts, so reading both tells you more.

exercises.prompt: Sort the facts: which text tells them?
exercises.hint: Text A is the fact page; text B is the diary.
items: It is dark nearly all day
exercises.explain: Only text A: the biggest penguins, the mother at sea. Only text B: −30 °C and the dark.

exercises.prompt: Sort the details: Story 1 or Story 2?
exercises.hint: Picture each story: a kite in the wind, a sled in the snow.
exercises.explain: Story 1: a windy park in spring, and a long stick. Story 2: a snowy hill in winter, and planks and rope.

exercises.prompt: Match each part of the two stories to how they compare.
exercises.hint: Look at each part in both stories: is it the same, alike, or different?
exercises.explain: The characters are the same (Pip and Nell). The settings are different (a park, a hill). The plots are alike (a problem, then help). The theme is the same (friends help each other).

exercises.prompt: Put the events of Story 1 in order.
items: The kite gets stuck in a tree.
exercises.hint: Start with Pip in the park, before anything goes wrong.
exercises.explain: Pip flies the kite, it gets stuck, Nell finds a stick, and together they shake it free: a problem, then a friend helps.

exercises.prompt: Sort the facts: in both penguin texts, or in only one?
items: The eggs sit on their feet.
exercises.hint: Look for each fact in text A, then in text B. Is it in both?
exercises.explain: Both say they live in Antarctica and the fathers keep the eggs warm on their feet. Only text A says emperors are the biggest; only text B gives −30 °C.
